PullRequest.Title: ci: reuse the shared node_modules cache in Monaco Editor checks
PullRequest.Body:

The **Monaco Editor checks** workflow now restores the `node_modules-compile` cache that [`pr-node-modules.yml`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/.github/workflows/pr-node-modules.yml) keeps warm on `main`, using `.github/actions/restore-node-modules`. It no longer saves any caches.

## Why

#342753 removed the `push: main` trigger from this workflow. Those push runs had also kept a `main`-scoped Monaco cache current, which every PR could reuse. After the next dependency change on `main`, that entry stopped matching. Now every Monaco PR run:

1. misses the exact key and partially restores the old `main` entry,
2. runs `npm ci`,
3. saves its **own** `Linux-cacheNodeModules20-*` (~1.5 GB) and `Linux-npmCacheDir-*` (~1.24 GB) entries. Only that PR can use them.

On 2026-10-20 that came to **~33 GB of the ~53 GB** on the [Actions caches page](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/caches): 24 PR-scoped Monaco entries across 13 PRs. This pushes out the shared `main` caches (`node_modules-*`, CodeQL overlay base, Electron…), so `pr-node-modules.yml` has to rebuild them more often.

## Changes

- Replace the two `actions/cache` steps (`**/node_modules` and the npm cache folder) with `restore-node-modules` using `key-prefix: node_modules-compile` and `key-args: "compile $(node -p process.arch)"`. These are the same inputs as the Compile job in `pr.yml`, so both share one cache entry.
- No `save-node-modules` step, so PR runs never write PR-scoped caches.
- On a miss (a PR that changes dependencies, or the window before `pr-node-modules.yml` rewarms after a dependency change lands), the existing system-dependencies install and `npm ci` steps still run.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Cross-runner restore:** this job runs on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`, while the cache is saved from the self-hosted 1ES Ubuntu pool. The cache version depends only on the path (`.build/node_modules_cache`), the compression method (zstd) and the OS (Linux), as mirrored in `detect-missing-caches/detect.ts`. So both runners compute the same version.
- **Contents:** the archive contains every `node_modules` folder in the repo (`listNodeModules.ts`), including `test/monaco`, which these checks use.
- **Trade-off:** a dependency-changing PR now runs a full `npm ci` with nothing cached, where before it partially restored from an older cache. That costs a few minutes in that case, in exchange for ~2.7 GB of storage per PR.
- The existing `Linux-cacheNodeModules20-*` / `Linux-npmCacheDir-*` entries will expire after 7 days unused, or get evicted sooner. They can also be deleted by hand.

## Validation

- Locally computed `computeNodeModulesCacheKey(['compile', 'x64'])` + `hashFiles` → `node_modules-compile-5e8e2f69bc8e…`, which matches the live `refs/heads/main` entry from `gh cache list -R microsoft/vscode --key node_modules-compile`. ✅
- YAML parses (`python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"`). ✅
- `actionlint`: not run (not available locally).
- To confirm on this PR: the "Restore node_modules cache" step of **Monaco Editor checks** should report a cache hit, and no new `Linux-cacheNodeModules20-*` / `Linux-npmCacheDir-*` entry should appear for this PR.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The miss and repetition behavior follows directly from the exact hashed key, main-only cache producer, release/dependency-changing triggers, and absence of any save step. The precise install duration varies by runner/network, but the PR description itself corroborates that a cold miss costs minutes; that uncertainty affects magnitude, not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: npm package downloads plus filesystem and install CPU work for the repository's full dependency tree
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The full `npm ci` is repeated once per Monaco workflow run for as many commits and reruns as a PR remains on a key that the main-only warmer never publishes; release-branch PRs can remain in this state indefinitely after their dependency graph diverges from main.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated multi-minute critical-path installs, increased network/filesystem load, and slower Monaco checks.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: On an exact miss, the workflow restored the latest node_modules/npm-cache prefix, ran `npm ci`, and `actions/cache` saved the resulting exact PR-scoped entries; later runs with the same dependency key skipped installation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new composite action restores only the exact `node_modules-compile` key and never saves. Because `pr-node-modules.yml` publishes that key only on pushes to `main`, a dependency-changing PR or a `release/*` PR with a different lockfile misses on every run and executes both apt installation and a cold `npm ci`.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 31 replaces the prior saving `actions/cache` path with the restore-only composite action; adjacent added lines 27-29 explicitly state that PR runs never save, and the deleted cache steps included both `restore-keys` fallbacks and automatic post-job saves.
Findings.Title: Keep a warm cache for non-main dependency keys
Findings.Impact: A PR that changes dependencies—and especially an active release-branch PR whose lockfile no longer matches main—pays the full dependency installation on every update or rerun instead of only the first miss, delaying required Monaco checks by minutes and repeatedly downloading packages.
Findings.Evidence: `computeNodeModulesCacheKey` hashes every dependency section and lockfile, while the replacement action uses an exact key with no restore keys and has no save step. The only saver for `node_modules-compile` is `pr-node-modules.yml`, whose trigger is `push` to `main`; this workflow also explicitly runs for `release/*`. The deleted `actions/cache` steps supplied prefix fallbacks and automatically saved exact node_modules and npm-cache entries after a successful miss.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the shared exact-hit path, but ensure supported non-main keys can become warm without restoring the old per-PR cache flood—for example, run the shared warmer for active `release/*` base branches and provide a bounded PR-local or shared npm-download fallback for dependency-changing keys.

Scenarios.Scenario: Monaco checks for a main-targeting PR whose dependency inputs match the warmed main key
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Checkout and Node setup are followed by one GitHub Actions cache restore and archive extraction; that restore must complete before all Monaco compile/test steps. On an exact hit, apt and `npm ci` remain off the path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore the shared `node_modules-compile` archive from GitHub Actions cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One exact-key cache restore per workflow run, serving every node_modules directory as one grouped archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The workflow restored one exact `**/node_modules` cache; on an exact hit it likewise skipped installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Download and extraction block every subsequent Monaco check, as the previous cache restoration did.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract the grouped node_modules zstd archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extraction per exact cache hit, independent of package count at the boundary though CPU/I/O scale with the full archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: `actions/cache` directly extracted its cached node_modules tree rather than invoking the repository's additional extraction action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Extraction must finish before checks run.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The archive contains all repository node_modules trees, but effective boundary cardinality is one grouped restore per run.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One restore/extraction within a job. This workflow has no run-level concurrency group, so multiple PR events can overlap, but that was already true.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm exact keys are published on main by `pr-node-modules.yml`; default-branch entries are reusable by PR runs. There is no prefix or negative-cache behavior in the new action.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the exact-hit call path and grouped cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Archive restore/extraction timing varies by GitHub cache locality and runner I/O; no evidence shows the composite extraction is slower overall than the former many-file cache path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression on the warm main-key path; the change reuses the shared cache and removes PR-scoped cache writes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dependency-changing main PR or release-branch PR whose dependency hash has no main-published exact cache
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The exact cache lookup misses, after which system package installation and a full `npm ci` must complete before any Monaco check can begin. Since this workflow never saves, the same path recurs on every commit or rerun until a matching main cache happens to be published; a divergent release key may never be published by the main-only warmer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exact-key GitHub Actions cache lookup/restore for `node_modules-compile`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lookup per run; zero archive downloads on an exact miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One node_modules lookup supported a prefix fallback; a prefix hit still installed dependencies but seeded the run, and a successful run saved an exact PR cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The miss gates entry into the apt and npm installation path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `sudo apt update` and install required system packages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One apt update/install sequence per cache-missing workflow run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This ran on the first exact miss, but subsequent runs with the exact PR-scoped node_modules cache skipped it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `npm ci`, fetching packages and writing the complete repository dependency tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full install per workflow run; npm performs package-level registry/download and filesystem work internally. Effective workflow multiplicity is the number of commits/reruns that retain the unpublished dependency key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The first exact miss restored an npm-cache prefix and then saved exact node_modules/npm entries, so later runs with the same key skipped installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks all Monaco compile and test steps and is the dominant cold-miss work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of PR updates/reruns sharing an unpublished dependency hash; installation cost also scales with the repository's full dependency graph, not merely Monaco packages.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each job serializes apt then one `npm ci`, but workflow runs and separate PRs have no shared limiter, so multiple cold installs can execute concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold misses are neither populated nor coalesced. Main dependency keys become warm only after the main push warmer runs; dependency-changing PR keys remain cold before merge, and release-specific keys have no configured producer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high confidence from the exact hash inputs, restore-only action, main-only producer, and release/dependency-changing triggers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact frequency of release divergence and number of updates per dependency PR vary, but the repeated miss mechanism is deterministic; cold-install duration is corroborated as minutes.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: every run repeats expensive installation where the old path became warm after a successful miss.

Scenarios.Scenario: Repository-wide Actions cache storage and shared-cache eviction pressure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PR runs no longer upload node_modules or npm cache archives after checks. Cache saving was post-job work and did not enable the current run, while evictions affected later CI runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upload PR-scoped node_modules and npm cache archives to GitHub Actions cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reduced by the diff from up to two large uploads on each old exact miss to zero uploads per Monaco PR run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both `actions/cache` steps scheduled post-job saves after misses, creating entries scoped to individual PR refs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removed from the job's completion path and no longer consumes shared cache capacity.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Previously scaled with the number of PRs/runs missing the exact old key and with the full node_modules/npm-cache byte size; now zero for this workflow.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent PR jobs can restore the shared entry but no longer race to upload separate entries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new workflow is restore-only and relies on one main-published exact archive, avoiding duplicate PR-scoped entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from replacing saving `actions/cache` actions with `actions/cache/restore` through the composite action.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact eviction timing depends on repository cache quotas and access patterns, but elimination of the writes is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement in storage, upload I/O, and shared-cache retention; no additional finding. Blame on the old cache lines resolved only a later SHA-pinning edit rather than the change that created the observed regression, so no regression-fix record was submitted.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed workflow. Traced exact hits, persistent misses, cache producers/consumers, install boundaries, release-branch behavior, storage writes, cardinality, and concurrency. Submitted one medium cache-lifecycle finding for repeated cold installs on unpublished dependency keys.
